title: Task 1: Parse Classes-chapter callouts
description:
Objective:
Add the focused structural parser that turns Classes-chapter gray callout boxes into deterministic `RuleExtraction` values without changing feature or subclass parsing.

Files:
- Create: `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseClassCallouts.ts`
- Create: `packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseClassCallouts.test.ts`

Steps:
1. Write a failing Vitest suite that imports `parseClassCallouts` and constructs `PageText` fixtures with `lineHeights`. Include Druid with two consecutive callouts, Paladin, Warlock, and Wizard; use regular heading heights above 11.5, callout headings at 10.8, normal body at 8.88/9.84, and following class headings to close bodies.
2. Assert the parser returns these sorted `(name, keySlug)` pairs: `Breaking Your Oath` / `paladin-breaking-your-oath`, `Druids and the Gods` / `druid-druids-and-the-gods`, `Sacred Plants and Wood` / `druid-sacred-plants-and-wood`, `Your Pact Boon` / `warlock-your-pact-boon`, `Your Spellbook` / `wizard-your-spellbook`.
3. Assert each body contains its own representative prose but excludes the next callout/class/feature text. Specifically ensure `Sacred Plants and Wood` excludes `Druids and the Gods`, while `Druids and the Gods` excludes the next class heading.
4. Assert source pages come from each callout heading and a uniform-font/no-height fixture emits no callouts, preserving fixture behavior.
5. Run `npx vitest run packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseClassCallouts.test.ts`. Expected RED: the new parser module/export does not exist.
6. Implement `parseClassCallouts(pages: readonly PageText[]): RuleExtraction[]`. Flatten normalized lines with page/height; return empty unless `hasHeadingTiers` passes; update current class on normalized names in `PARENT_CLASS_NAMES`; identify headings with `isCalloutBoxHeading`; collect following lines only while their defined height is lower than the detected callout heading height, so a same-tier callout or any larger feature/subclass/class heading closes the body without duplicating a font threshold; join trimmed lines into paragraph-preserving text; emit `keySlug` as `<class-slug>-<title-slug>`; sort by name.
7. Run the focused test again. Expected GREEN: all parser tests pass.
8. Run `npx biome check packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseClassCallouts.ts packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseClassCallouts.test.ts`. Expected: no diagnostics.
9. Commit with `git add packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseClassCallouts.ts packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseClassCallouts.test.ts && git commit -m "feat(srd): parse class callout boxes"`.
design:
Use existing structural helpers from `parseSubclasses.ts`: `hasHeadingTiers`, `isCalloutBoxHeading`, and `PARENT_CLASS_NAMES`. Do not key behavior on the five title strings; the exact title/key set is enforced later by importer coverage. Suggested public signature:

```ts
export function parseClassCallouts(
  pages: readonly PageText[],
): RuleExtraction[]
```

The parser owns only headings accepted by `isCalloutBoxHeading`. For each accepted heading, body lines continue while their height is lower than that heading’s height; a same-tier callout or any larger heading closes the body. Undefined heights are allowed only after the slice has passed `hasHeadingTiers`, and should be treated as body for defensive compatibility. This avoids exporting or duplicating the font-band constants. Inline prose lead-ins such as `Copying a Spell into the Book.` remain body. Prefixing keys with the current class prevents collisions and preserves lookup context without adding schema fields.
acceptance_criteria: Focused parser tests pass; exactly five real-shaped callouts have class-qualified keys, correct pages, isolated text, deterministic ordering; uniform-font fixtures emit none; no title whitelist; changed files pass Biome; commit created.
close_reason: Focused structural class-callout parser and regression tests implemented; spec and quality reviews approved; focused/nearby tests and Biome passed.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: Debug evidence: npm run verify:worktree reproducibly reaches npm run typecheck and fails at parseClassCallouts.ts:79 with TS18048 because heading.height is optional. The runtime isCalloutBoxHeading boolean rejects undefined, but its return type is not a TypeScript type predicate, so control-flow analysis cannot narrow heading.height. Existing parsers avoid relying on that narrowing. Hypothesis: capture heading.height and explicitly reject undefined before the predicate; this preserves runtime behavior and gives the comparison a number type.

comments.text: Spec review item 1 accepted: parseClassCallouts.ts changes class context on any exact base-class name, while PR #163 added isParentClassHeading to reject low-height table/body occurrences such as the Oath spell-table 'Paladin' cell. Fix required: add a failing regression fixture proving a low-height class-name line does not reattribute the next callout, then use isParentClassHeading(line, height, tiersPresent).

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: Review evaluation: accepted. parseClassCallouts currently uses PARENT_CLASS_NAMES.has for context changes, unlike parseSubclasses and parseFeatures, so multi-tier extraction can treat a body/table cell at height 8.88 as a class chapter heading. Regression target: a real chapter heading followed by a low-height Paladin cell and then a callout must retain the real chapter context.
